title.narrative: Catalyst for Change: Empowering Grassroots Civil Society

description.narrative: BRAC's Integrated Development Programme (IDP) has secured Sida's support to implement Catalyst for Change: Empowering Grassroots Civil Society, a two-year project (May 2026 - 30 April 2028) that supports about ten (10) community-based organisations (CBOs) and their constituencies in the climate-vulnerable, socially isolated Barind region of northern Bangladesh. The programme is concentrated in Naogaon district, home to the largest concentration of plainland indigenous people in the Barind tract, where poverty rates reach as high as 80 percent and literacy rates remain as low as 17-25 percent among indigenous communities. Climate-induced droughts, over-extraction of groundwater, and a shift from paddy to mango cultivation are eroding the already limited agricultural day-labour opportunities on which indigenous women depend, deepening both economic and social exclusion.Catalyst for Change works through BRAC's Village Development Organisations (VDOs), which will be organised, capacitated, and connected to become formally registered CBOs. In line with BRAC's Theory of Change, the programme asserts that sustained resilience among marginalised communities is driven by four factors: strengthened CBO governance and organisational capacity; enhanced socio-economic agency of CBO constituencies; shifts in community attitudes and practices through effective advocacy; and knowledge-sharing for continuous learning and adaptation.

To establish diverse formal and informal community-based organisations (CBOs) that drive inclusive societies and sustainable economic resilience among marginalised indigenous communities in Naogaon, Bangladesh.

participating-org.narrative: Sweden, through Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida)
